methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops led by a Norfolk native directly target the technology gap through peer-based skill transfer, signaling grassroots capacity building that could distribute deep fluency beyond traditional tech hubs if sustained and scaled.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's partnership with AI Ready RVA creates institutional infrastructure for community-wide AI education and innovation, potentially seeding distributed deep capability through regional anchor institutions rather than concentrating expertise in NoVA alone.

signals.title: TAYLOR: AI data centers increase Virginia’s urban-rural divide - The Cavalier Daily
signals.signal_reading: Opinion piece explicitly naming data centers as drivers of urban-rural divide signals that AI infrastructure concentration in NoVA may extract resources (land, power, water) while exporting little capability, reinforcing rather than bridging geographic inequality.

signals.title: Norfolk Southern deploys AI system to catch wheel defects before they break - The Business Journals
signals.signal_reading: Norfolk Southern's deployment of sophisticated AI defect-detection systems demonstrates deep technical capability in Hampton Roads' rail/logistics sector, but signals enterprise-owned expertise rather than workforce-level fluency that could distribute across the region.

signals.title: Three-day workshop to explore use of AI in project management - Virginia Tech News
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech's three-day AI workshop for project management professionals signals practical skill-building outside NoVA, potentially distributing applied AI fluency through professional networks in a historically underserved region if it moves beyond one-off events to sustained capability development.
